title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
abstract: arXiv:2611.14211v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Software agents built on large language models generate traffic unlike human web traffic, yet routers have no class for it and cannot verify a sender's claim to be an agent. This paper proposes the Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class (VATC), which combines a reserved Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) value declaring agent traffic, a router-side classifier that demotes flows contradicting the declaration to a class served after best-effort traffic, and a rate-limited priority queue. VATC was compared with static Differentiated Services (DiffServ), a dedicated class that trusts the marking, and fq_codel, a per-flow fair-queuing scheduler, in two simulators and on a real Linux kernel. VATC matched DiffServ under steady load. In a constructed burst it cut mean agent queuing delay by 98% relative to DiffServ in simulation (assuming an immediate verdict), at a 12% increase in human delay; most of the gain came from the separate class. translated_title: 可验证智能体流量类别：一种面向智能体AI流量的受管控服务质量机制，从仿真到真实内核对抗性测试的评估
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型构建的软件智能体所产生的流量与人类网页流量截然不同，然而路由器尚无针对此类流量的类别，也无法验证发送方声称自己是智能体的真实性。本文提出了可验证智能体流量类别（VATC），它结合了三项机制：一个用于声明智能体流量的保留差分服务代码点（DSCP）值、一个路由器侧分类器（将与声明不符的流量降级至在尽力而为流量之后服务的类别），以及一个速率受限的优先队列。研究在两个仿真器和一个真实的Linux内核上，将VATC与静态差分服务DiffServ（一种信任标记的专用类别）以及fq_codel（一种每流公平排队调度器）进行了对比。结果表明，VATC在稳定负载下与DiffServ表现相当；在构造的突发流量场景中，VATC在仿真环境下（假设即时判定）相比DiffServ将智能体平均排队延迟降低了98%，而人类流量的延迟仅增加12%，其中大部分收益来自于独立类别的设计。
tldr: 本文提出可验证智能体流量类别（VATC），通过DSCP流量声明、路由器侧验证分类器和速率受限优先队列，为智能体AI流量提供可验证的服务质量保障，在突发场景下相比传统DiffServ将智能体排队延迟降低98%，同时仅使人类流量延迟增加12%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class (VATC), which combines a DSCP traffic declaration, a router-side verifying classifier, and a rate-limited priority queue to provide verifiable quality-of-service for agentic AI traffic, cutting agent queuing delay by 98% versus DiffServ under bursty conditions at only a 12% increase in human delay.
